critical_issues: Severe highlight clipping/overexposure in the core (pure white with hard transitions), which kills fire detail and looks non-physical.
warnings: (Most important) Switch to an actual explosion workflow: simulate/render a volumetric fire+smoke element (pyro/VDB) and drive emission from temperature/heat, not from flat emissive geometry.
Adopt HDR + proper tonemapping: render to 16/32-bit EXR and use Filmic/ACES so the core stays bright without clipping; add bloom/glare in comp rather than letting the beauty pass blow out.

Build a two-layer volume: (1) short-lived luminous flame volume (high emission, lower absorption), (2) longer-lived darker smoke volume (higher absorption, more scattering) with internal self-shadowing.
Add multi-scale turbulence: combine low-frequency large lobes + higher-frequency detail noise so the silhouette becomes “cauliflower/mushroom cloud” rather than sharp/rectilinear shapes.
Add secondary particles: embers/sparks (additive, short lifetime) + fine dust/ash (longer lifetime) + a range of debris sizes; enable motion blur for fast fragments in animation renders.
Improve scene lighting response: ensure the explosion actually lights nearby objects (warm fill/rim, spec hits on surfaces) and that smoke/volume casts shadows onto the environment.

If you must iterate within the current script/material (glass/shatter look):
- Line 341 (Metallic 0.6): reduce toward 0.0–0.1 for glass-like shards; high metallic reads wrong for debris.
- Line 446 (Base Color): push closer to neutral/grey and rely on transmission/refraction rather than bright diffuse tint.
- Line 209 (Bump Distance 0.1): reduce (e.g., 0.01–0.03) to avoid chunky surface breakup on shards.
- Lines 105–106 (BG Color/Strength): keep background darker but slightly raise environment contribution only if you need scene readability; avoid using BG to “fake” explosion brightness.
- Noise scales (187–195, 242–243, 264, 366): use them for subtle roughness/imperfection variation, not for large-scale ‘explosion’ structure (explosion structure should come from volumetrics/sim).

For quality control, compare against an explosion reference each iteration (the auto-picked reference scored ~20/100 similarity here); aim for visible smoke volume, warm core gradient, and layered detail before tuning debris/shading.
